title: Clinical Documentation and Shared Care Record Agent

approval.note: A composed script is a draft. A human reads it before this film is published anywhere.

script.vo01: Clinicians write the record after the encounter, often after the day has ended, and documentation competes with the next patient. Emergency crews describe what happened twice - once in the moment and again in the write-up.
script.vo02: Health information sits with the provider who collected it, so the next clinician starts without the context.
script.vo03: It reads Consultation notes and dictation, Encounter audio. It engages you in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams. And it can draft the clinical note from the consultation itself, showing the reasoning behind every answer.
script.vo04: A clinician asks for the consultation note. The agent drafts it from the encounter itself, structured the way the record expects, with every clinical statement traceable back to what was said.
script.vo05: Asked about follow-up, the agent lists the actions captured during the consultation, the referrals implied by them, and the items that need the clinician to confirm before anything is sent.
script.vo06: On risk, the agent marks what it inferred rather than heard, highlights anything a clinician must verify, and leaves the note unsigned until a person reviews it.
script.vo_payoff: Clinicians leave the encounter with the note already drafted and their attention still on the patient.
script.vo_helps: The result? Documentation lifted off the clinician, one capture instead of a second write-up, and care context that travels with the patient.
script.vo_cta: Get started on your agentic journey today. Talk to your Microsoft representative to learn more.
